Hi Amir / Sam / team,

Thanks — happy to confirm the items below. Short answers first, then a couple of implementation notes.

1) Controller / Processor
- Confirmation: Cascade Financial is the Controller and Redwood Inference acts as a Processor for data transmitted to our inference API. Redwood does not make independent decisions about purposes and means of processing customer data in this use case.

2) Subprocessors
- Current subprocessors include our cloud provider (AWS), managed observability (Grafana Cloud), and our CDN partner. We maintain a living subprocessors list at: https://redwood.ai/subprocessors (public).
- Notification / objection: We notify customers of material additions and provide a 30-day objection window for reasonable security/privacy concerns; in practice we rarely see objections.

3) Breach notice
- Our standard practice is to provide initial notification within 72 hours of detection for incidents that materially affect customer PII. We recognize Cascade prefers 48 hours; we can commit to 48 hours for enterprise customers under a written SLA amendment (can be included in Dedicated or Private deployments).

4) Data residency
- We support region-specific hosting (US and EU zones) for both inference and log storage. For EU-origin data we can restrict processing and backups to EU zones when customer chooses the EU region option (requires Dedicated or Private deployment for stricter guarantees).

5) Retention & logging controls
- Default request/response log retention (for hosted API) is 30 days. Audit logs (control-plane events) are retained for 90 days by default.
- Enterprise customers can configure retention windows or request shorter retention via contractual terms for Dedicated/Private deployments. We also offer a config to redact or not persist certain PII fields at ingestion.

Implementation notes and attachments:
- Encryption: All customer data in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256) — keys managed via KMS; for Private deployments customers can bring their own KMS.
- Access controls: Role-based access and least-privilege for access to production logs; access is logged and audited.
- Subprocessor detail: full list + datacenters is on the link above; we can provide SOC2 reports under NDA.

Attached is an excerpt of our DPA with the clauses referenced (Redwood_DPA_excerpt.pdf). If Cascade legal has specific redlines, send them back and we will ingest and propose counter-redlines. If you'd like, we can set a 30-minute follow-up call with our counsel to walk through any contested language.

Hope this helps — happy to expand on any item.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Head of Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
